say.text: Cairo, in the days after the emirs came over.
You said one thing to al-Mashtub, another to my uncle, a third to Qutb ad-Din. I listened to each of them, and each was true. Which was your own?
All three. A man with one reason to follow you will leave when the reason does. A man with three will stay.
You spoke to Qutb ad-Din of origins. I was not easy about that.

I said what he could hear, as I said to the others. It was not a promise from you. Do not be easy about it: be careful with it. The day you need men of every kind, you will be glad you never asked who their grandfathers were.
That is a better argument than the one you used.
It is the same argument, my lord. I only told the part of it he could hear.
